name: chrome-bridge-mcp

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Status of the bridge itself, not of a page: call it when a tool you expect is missing or browser commands fail (connected=false: the extension is not reachable, extension_install gives its Chrome Web Store link). Also reports mode (primary/relay), host, port, server and extension versions, js_evaluation (false under --no-js), write_root, read_root, session_tab_id (the implicit tab), owned_tabs (created by this session), uptime_sec. caps_active and caps_available: a missing tool lives in an inactive cap. enable is the only change it makes: it switches caps on for this session, no restart, and lists the tools added. Optional caps: audits (cookie_audit); visual (inject_css, measure_spacing, emulate_media, viewport_resize); perf (animations, frames, perf_trace, screencast, lighthouse, heap_snapshot); network (http_auth, set_geolocation, track_events); storage (get_storage, set_storage, session_fixture); dom (modify_dom, watch_dom, drag_and_drop); files (save_page, manage_downloads, session_record).

enable.description: Caps to switch on now, all in one call; "all" = every cap

tools.name: get_tabs
tools.description: List every open tab with id, url, title, active flag and mine (created by this session). Find a tab_id when the implicit target is not the one you mean. include_windows adds position, size, state and type of each window — needed before moving or tiling. Session tabs gone since the last call come back once in closed_session_tabs with the reason (closed, window_closed, replaced, closed_by_bridge).

include_windows.description: Also return the windows with bounds, state, type and tab count

tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Navigate a Chrome tab to a URL and wait for the load; DNS and connection errors fail the call. Without tab_id it reuses the tab this session last navigated or created, else opens a new one rather than taking over the active tab. Returns a preview of interactive elements with refs usable in click/type_text/hover, plus the first console errors and failed requests, if any.

url.description: Absolute URL, or a path resolved against the current page

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Screenshot of the visible viewport only (PNG), at the current scroll position, or one per viewport preset with presets. Read-only. Activates the tab in the background without stealing window focus, then restores the previous tab. Downscaled to ≤1568px: for fine print, element_screenshot with scale.

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

save_to.description: Absolute path: write the PNG there and return the path instead of the content

presets.description: Resizes the window per preset, then restores it; not phone emulation. A refused width is reported, not shot. save_to = directory

if_changed.description: Same pixels as the last screenshot of this tab: a note instead of the image. false = always send it

tools.name: execute_js
tools.description: Run JavaScript in the page (MAIN world). Requires the extension's "Allow user scripts" toggle; errors explain setup if disabled. Use it when no dedicated tool fits: extract or extract_table read data, query_dom inspects elements, inject_css restyles, and none of them needs the toggle. A promise is awaited up to timeout. A cut result stays valid JSON and says truncated; save_to writes the whole result to disk.

code.description: JS evaluated in the page; the value of the last expression is returned

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

timeout.description: Max ms to wait for the result (default 30000); raise it for long async work

save_to.description: Absolute path: write the result (a string as is, anything else as JSON) there and return the path instead of the content

tools.name: click
tools.description: Click an element by CSS selector or by a ref (n1, n2…) from get_interactives or navigate. A real pointer sequence: it can submit, open a dialog or navigate — use wait_after. Not idempotent; a native confirm() blocks the bridge: handle_dialogs first. Returns page_changed (url, title and DOM deltas: nodes, text, open, expanded, checked, dialogs, focus): the effect, without a screenshot; when the click opens or reveals something, the refs of the visible interactives follow, no get_interactives needed.

selector.description: CSS selector; ">>>" pierces shadow DOM. Ignored when ref is given

button.description: right opens the page context menu instead of activating the element

count.description: 2 emits dblclick after the two clicks, which is what selects a word or opens an editor

trusted.description: Real browser input (isTrusted) via chrome.debugger, main frame only: for widgets that ignore synthetic clicks

wait_after.description: Settle before returning: navigation waits for a page load, networkidle for quiet traffic

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

tools.name: type_text
tools.description: Put text into an input, textarea or contenteditable, by selector or ref. Replaces the whole value through the native setter (React/Vue controlled inputs register it) and fires input and change. mode=keys emits keydown/input/keyup per character for autocomplete and masked fields: slower, use it only when mode=set leaves the field empty. Returns value_after; mismatch=true means the field did not keep the value: retry with mode=keys.

selector.description: CSS selector; ">>>" pierces shadow DOM. Ignored when ref is given

text.description: Value to type; empty string clears the field

mode.description: set = assign value; keys = per-char events (autocomplete/masked); trusted = real input via chrome.debugger, main frame

wait_after.description: Settle before returning: navigation waits for a page load, networkidle for quiet traffic

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Read the page as text (default), markdown, raw HTML, or accessibility tree. Read-only. markdown keeps headings, links and tables at a fraction of the HTML cost. Expensive on big pages: HTML on a large table costs tens of thousands of tokens for data you filter anyway — prefer extract_table/extract for repeated content, get_interactives for click targets.

mode.description: text strips markup; markdown keeps headings/links/tables far cheaper than html; accessibility = a11y tree

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

save_to.description: Absolute path: write the page there and return the path instead of the content

tools.name: get_page_info
tools.description: Page metadata: title, url, visibility, doctype, charset, meta tags, scripts, stylesheets, links and forms. visibility=hidden means the window is minimized, covered or in the background: the page does not render (screenshots fail) and its timers slow down. dev.server names a dev server (vite, webpack-dev-server, next, nuxt) and dev.overlay carries the compiler message when an error overlay is open: read it before treating the page as valid. For the text use read_page, for specific elements query_dom, for the bridge itself get_status.

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

tools.name: query_dom
tools.description: Query DOM elements by CSS selector, returning structure, attributes, bounding rect and, with properties, computed styles. Use it when you already have a selector (no match: count 0); to find one, get_interactives or find_text; for the rule that set a style, get_css_styles.

selector.description: CSS selector; ">>>" pierces shadow DOM. Matches all, not just the first

limit.description: Max elements returned, from the top of the match list

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

tools.name: get_css_styles
tools.description: Why an element looks the way it does: for each CSS property the winning declaration — selector, stylesheet, rule position, !important, @layer, @media — and the ones it overrides, like the Styles panel of DevTools; query_dom gives the computed value, this gives who set it. Read-only, from the CSSOM: stylesheets of another origin without CORS are opaque and listed by href; user-agent styles, @container and @scope rules are not evaluated. properties narrows the output.

selector.description: CSS selector; ">>>" pierces shadow DOM. Only the first match is inspected

properties.description: Only these, e.g. ["margin-top","--brand"]; margin covers its longhands. Omitted = every property a matching rule sets

include_inherited.description: Also inherited properties (color, font-*, custom properties) with the ancestor that sets them

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

tools.name: read_console
tools.description: Read console messages captured since page load, incl. uncaught errors and unhandled rejections. clear deletes the messages it returns, hence not read-only; since=cursor reads only newer ones without deleting, and failed requests are in monitor_network.

level.description: all merges every level in one chronological list

format.description: lines is compact; json keeps timestamps and stack traces

sourcemap.description: Resolve bundle.js:line:col frames to source files through their source maps

since.description: cursor from the previous read: only newer entries, nothing deleted

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: monitor_network
tools.description: Monitor network requests. source=page: XHR/fetch hook (installed on first call); source=browser: all requests incl. static assets; source=websocket: connections and messages. format=har exports HAR 1.2. It only observes: to block, stub or rewrite requests use network_rules, to send one yourself http_request.

source.description: page: XHR/fetch only; browser: static assets too; websocket: connections and messages

format.description: har exports HAR 1.2 for external tooling

since.description: cursor from the previous read: only newer entries, nothing deleted

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: create_tab
tools.description: Open a new tab, optionally at a URL, and make it the implicit target of later commands in this session. Each call creates another tab: reuse a tab_id or navigate() to move an existing one instead of piling up tabs.

url.description: URL to open (default: new tab page)

active.description: false opens the tab in the background, leaving the current one focused

new_window.description: Open in a fresh window instead of a tab; with left/top it lands on the chosen monitor

left.description: Window x on the virtual desktop (new_window)

tools.name: wait_for
tools.description: Block until a condition holds: element, text, function (JS expression; needs the "Allow user scripts" toggle), navigation (mode=spa for client-side routes), network_idle. Polls until timeout (10s element/function, 15s the rest) then **returns `found: false` with a reason instead of raising**: check it, or a failed wait reads as success. Read-only.

condition.description: element and text need selector or text; function needs expression

selector.description: condition=element; with condition=text it narrows the search to that subtree

text.description: Literal text to wait for (condition=text), matched case-insensitively

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

tools.name: scroll
tools.description: Scroll. action=to: once to element/coordinates; action=until: repeatedly until element visible, network idle, or no new content (infinite scroll). It moves the tab's scroll position and returns it (to) or stopped_reason and steps (until); full_page_screenshot scrolls by itself, wait_for waits without scrolling.

action.description: to jumps to a position or element; until scrolls repeatedly to load more

x.description: Absolute horizontal position in px (action=to, without selector)

y.description: Absolute vertical position in px (action=to, without selector)

behavior.description: instant avoids waiting for smooth-scroll animations

until.description: no_new_content stops when the page height stops growing

max_scrolls.description: Cap on scroll steps, so an infinite feed terminates

step_px.description: px per step, default viewport height

container.description: until: selector that scrolls; default the document, or the largest scrollable element if the document does not scroll

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

tools.name: fill_form
tools.description: Batch fill form fields with React-compatible events. Handles input, select, checkbox, radio, and textarea. Fields and submit take a CSS selector or a ref (n1, n2…) from navigate/get_interactives. With submit_selector it also submits, so a repeated call submits twice — not safe to retry blindly; after a submit, after_submit carries url, title and the text the page gained (the confirmation or the errors). Each field reports value_after and mismatch; page_changed carries the DOM delta, and the refs of what appeared.

selector.description: CSS selector; ignored when ref is given

value.description: Text, option value or label; for checkbox/radio "true"/"false"

checked.description: Checkbox/radio instead of value: true checks, false unchecks

fields.description: {selector or ref, value or checked} per field

submit_selector.description: Submit button to click after filling

submit_ref.description: Submit button as a ref, instead of submit_selector

wait_after.description: Settle before returning: navigation waits for a page load, networkidle for quiet traffic

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

tools.name: element_screenshot
tools.description: Screenshot cropped to one element or to a viewport region (PNG), optionally enlarged. Read-only. The cheapest image in the set, because it carries only the box you asked for — and with scale the way to read fine print: crop the box, zoom it, verify.

selector.description: CSS selector; ">>>" pierces shadow DOM. The element is scrolled into view first

region.description: Box in viewport CSS px (the rect frame of get_interactives/query_dom), instead of selector

scale.description: Enlargement of the crop, 1-4; output still capped at 1568px

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: full_page_screenshot
tools.description: Full-page capture by scrolling: stitched segments of ~2 viewports (≤1568px), or one image per viewport with stitch=false. Expensive: ~2.7k image tokens per segment, only max_segments returned, the rest via segment_offset. Reading the text you need is cheaper by an order of magnitude — prefer read_page, extract or find_text unless layout is the question.

max_scrolls.description: Cap on scroll steps: a taller page is captured only up to here

max_segments.description: Images returned from the top (≈2.7k image tokens each); segment_offset for the rest

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: hover
tools.description: Hover over an element, by CSS selector or ref. Default: synthetic mouseenter/mouseover/mousemove, which fire JS hover handlers but not CSS :hover. trusted moves the real mouse pointer (chrome.debugger), so CSS :hover rules and their transitions apply.

trusted.description: Real browser pointer via chrome.debugger, main frame only: needed for CSS :hover

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

tools.name: press_key
tools.description: Send a key to the focused element (or to selector, focusing it first) as a real keydown/keypress/keyup sequence, so framework handlers fire. For typing a value use type_text; this is for Enter, Tab, Escape, arrows and shortcuts. Not idempotent: two calls send the key twice. Returns page_changed like click; when the key opens or reveals something, the refs of the visible interactives follow.

trusted.description: Real browser key (isTrusted) via chrome.debugger, main frame only

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

frame_id.description: Target iframe id from get_frames; omitted = main frame

tools.name: get_frames
tools.description: List frames (main + iframes) with frameId, parent, URL — for the frame_id parameter of DOM tools.

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: tab_action
tools.description: Tab lifecycle: close, activate, reload, back, forward, discard, mute, duplicate, close_session (only tabs this session created). close drops unsaved work and cannot be undone — it may be the user's tab. reload drops injected CSS, emulations and hooks. duplicate works where create_tab is forbidden (chrome-untrusted://) and lands in the source window, app windows included. discard replaces the tab id.

action.description: close cannot be undone; discard frees memory (reloads on focus); reload drops injected CSS and hooks

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: upload_file
tools.description: Set a file on input[type=file] from the server filesystem via DataTransfer (max 200 MB; over 6 MB it travels in pieces). Keys and credentials (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.gnupg, .env*, *.pem, *.key, id_*…) are refused, and a --read-root on the server limits the readable tree: the call fails with an error, nothing is read.

selector.description: The file input to fill; ">>>" pierces shadow DOM

path.description: Absolute path on the server machine; keys and credentials (~/.ssh, .env, *.pem) refused

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: dismiss_overlays
tools.description: Dismiss cookie banners/modal overlays: OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, then generic heuristic. Idempotent.

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: handle_dialogs
tools.description: Auto-accept/dismiss future JS dialogs (alert/confirm/prompt), logging them. reset restores native dialogs and returns the log.

action.description: accept/dismiss auto-answer future dialogs; reset restores native behaviour

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: find_text
tools.description: Find text on the page: parent selector, context, visibility, position per match. Attaches nearby interactive elements (with refs for click/type_text/hover) for the first visible match. Use it when you know the words on screen but not the selector (query_dom needs one); no match returns count 0.

text.description: Literal text to find, not a regex

max_results.description: Cap on matches returned, in document order

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: network_rules
tools.description: Network interception, browser-wide, survives reloads until cleared: block, redirect, set/remove headers, stub a synthetic body, or record real API responses and replay them with forced errors/latency (local helper; from HTTPS pages the stub host must be trusted). It changes traffic, while monitor_network only observes it and http_request sends one request; each rule comes back as added, list shows them, clear removes them all.

action.description: record saves the page's API responses (url_filter) as a fixture, replay serves them with overrides; list/clear

overrides.description: replay: force a status, body or delay on matching URLs — error states a real backend will not produce

header_target.description: response = strip content-security-policy / x-frame-options, inject CORS

resource_types.description: Limit the rule to these request types; omitted = all of them

tools.name: screenshot_diff
tools.description: Visual regression: save a named baseline (viewport, element, or a PNG such as the design mockup) and compare later — changed-pixel % and a red-highlighted diff; or compare_urls: production vs staging in this tab, pixels plus text diff, logged-in pages included. Baselines are in-memory (lost on service worker restart).

action.description: baseline stores, compare measures against it, compare_urls diffs url_a vs url_b here, clear drops baselines

name.description: Baseline id: reuse the same one to compare across runs

from_file.description: action=baseline: take it from this PNG (design mockup) instead of capturing

url_b.description: compare_urls: page under test, e.g. staging or a PR preview

mask.description: compare_urls: selectors hidden on both pages (dates, carousels, ads)

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: handoff
tools.description: Hand the browser to the user for what only a person can do — 2FA, CAPTCHA, login, a choice — and wait: a banner in the page shows your message with Done/Cancel, the call returns on click or timeout, redirects included. pick_element: the user clicks an element and you get its selector. Never type credentials yourself. ask: the user types a reply in the banner ("which of the three?") and you get it as answer. pick_max: with pick_element, up to N elements; the user presses Done when finished.

message.description: What the user should do, one line

pick_element.description: Ask the user to click an element; returns its selector, text and box

ask.description: Show a text box in the banner; the reply comes back as answer

pick_max.description: With pick_element: up to N elements, the user presses Done when finished

timeout.description: ms to wait for the click, default 5 min

in_terminal.description: Also ask in the Claude Code terminal (MCP elicitation) when the client supports it; the first answer wins. Not for pick_element

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: watch
tools.description: Keep watching a page in the background — "tell me when the pipeline is green / the Approve button appears / this number changes" — checked every interval_s by the extension. Events are collected, not pushed: action=poll, or a script blocking on "chrome-bridge watch --wait <name>". Survives extension idling, not a browser restart. poll returns one line per event (time, name, kind, url, value, previous); a change due within seconds is wait_for.

until.description: Default: change with value_of, else match

reload.description: Reload before each check, for pages that do not update live

since.description: poll: events after this ms timestamp

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: read_form
tools.description: Read a form as the user filled it — label, type, value, checked/selected, required-but-empty, browser validity — to check it against the project's documents before an irreversible Submit. Password and card values come back [redacted]. Read-only, on request; to change values use fill_form.

selector.description: The form or container; omitted = every visible control on the page

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: audit
tools.description: One-call page audit, pick the kinds: accessibility, keyboard (tab order and focus issues), SEO, security headers, broken links, Core Web Vitals, unused CSS, resources (which plugin/theme/module/host slows the page), cache (is the CDN serving the new version). A summary line per kind; with save_to the full Markdown report with every finding. Read-only. For one deep look at load speed use perf_trace, for Lighthouse scores lighthouse.

kinds.description: Default skips keyboard, css (slow, approximate), resources and cache

save_to.description: Absolute path: write the full Markdown report there and return the path instead of the content

scope.description: a11y only: limit to this subtree

max_links.description: links only: cap on URLs fetched

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: find_setting
tools.description: Where is a setting in an unknown admin panel: follows the panel's menu links (same origin) until a page contains the keyword. Returns the URL, the menu path (Settings › Media) and the matching text; when nothing matches, how many pages it tried. Navigates the tab and leaves it on the last page visited, at most max_pages.

keyword.description: What you are looking for, e.g. "webp", "cron", "maintenance mode"

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: extract_table
tools.description: Read a real <table> as JSON: thead cells become keys, each row an object. Only for tabular markup — `where` filters rows server-side, so one matching row out of 1500 costs a few hundred bytes instead of the whole document. `row_count` is the table total, `match_count` how many rows passed the filter. No table at index is an error saying how many the selector found; for cards and lists use extract.

selector.description: The table to read; ">>>" pierces shadow DOM

index.description: Which table to take when the selector matches several, 0-based

max_rows.description: Max rows returned to you (output cap).

where.description: {column: substring} rows must match, case-insensitive (names too). Key "any" matches any cell.

columns.description: Return only these columns per row.

offset.description: Skip N rows of the (filtered) set before applying max_rows.

scan_rows.description: Max rows materialized in-page to scan/filter; raise for very large tables.

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: clipboard
tools.description: Read or write the system clipboard (text). Activates the tab and focuses its window first. write overwrites whatever the user had copied, which is not recoverable. To fill a field use type_text instead of write and paste; read checks what a Copy button copied, and an empty clipboard returns text "".

action.description: write takes text; read returns the current clipboard contents

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: capture_downloads
tools.description: Save files the page builds itself, with no browser download and no "Save as" dialog: blob and data URL links (a[download]), window.showSaveFilePicker writes, and downloads the page starts (cancelled at once, bytes fetched again with the browser cookies). arm with save_dir, then click Export/Download, then wait: it returns the saved paths. A file with a URL: http_request save_to instead. Names are cleaned, existing files never overwritten, size capped by max_mb.

action.description: arm before the click; wait returns what arrived and stays armed; disarm restores the page

save_dir.description: arm: absolute directory for the files; created if missing

max_mb.description: arm: per-file cap in MB (default 100, max 200); a bigger file is skipped

timeout.description: wait: max ms for the first file

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

tools.name: http_request
tools.description: HTTP request sent from the browser, with the logged-in user's cookies: fetches what a server-side request gets a login page for (invoices, authenticated JSON, exports). Text bodies inline (capped by max_length); save_to writes the bytes — the way to read a PDF, since read_page returns nothing on a PDF tab, and the way to save any file that has a URL: no click on Download, no browser download, no "Save as" dialog.

url.description: Absolute URL. Cookies are sent for its origin

method.description: HEAD fetches headers only, without the body

save_to.description: Absolute path: write the response bytes here instead of returning them (PDF, images, archives)

max_length.description: Max chars of body returned inline

tools.name: move_tab
tools.description: Move an existing tab into another window (chrome.tabs.move), keeping id, history and page state; works on chrome-untrusted:// tabs too. The **destination** must be a normal window: out of an app/popup window is fine, into one is refused. A ChromeOS Terminal tab can be pulled out (new_window, window_type popup) but never merged back: extensions cannot create app windows.

tab_id.description: Tab to move; get it from get_tabs

window_id.description: Destination window; get_tabs reports windowId for every tab

new_window.description: Extract the tab into a fresh window instead of an existing one

window_type.description: new_window only: popup has no tab strip nor omnibox, the terminal-window look

index.description: Position in the destination window; -1 appends at the end

tools.name: tile_windows
tools.description: Tile Chrome windows over one monitor in equal parts with no gap. Only Chrome windows. The monitor is the one of a window already on it, whose work area is read from a page there: at least one target needs a scriptable tab (not chrome://). Maximized windows are restored first, since maximized ignores bounds. To restore a saved arrangement use window_layout; to move one tab into another window, move_tab.

window_ids.description: Windows to tile; omitted = every normal window on the reference monitor

reference_window_id.description: Window whose monitor is used; omitted = the focused one

layout.description: columns splits left to right, rows top to bottom, grid keeps tiles as square as it can

padding.description: Px of empty margin kept inside the work area

include_types.description: Window types to include; omitted = normal only

area.description: Monitor area to fill, when no target window has a scriptable tab to read it from

tools.name: window_layout
tools.description: Save the current window arrangement under a name, restore, list or delete. save overwrites silently. Window ids do not survive a browser restart: restore matches windows by the overlap of their tab URLs and reports the ones it cannot recognise instead of guessing.

action.description: save snapshots every window; restore repositions the recognised ones

name.description: Layout name, required except for list

tools.name: get_interactives
tools.description: List actionable elements (buttons, links, inputs, [role], [onclick]) with ready-to-use CSS selector, label, position, flags. Prefer this over dumping HTML to discover selectors. Document order, cut at limit (count equal to limit: there may be more), each with a ref (n1, n2…) for click, type_text and hover.

limit.description: Max elements returned; raise it on a dense page

visible_only.description: false also lists elements hidden or scrolled out of view

format.description: lines is compact; json adds full attributes per element

since.description: cursor from the previous list: only added (+), changed (~) and removed elements; same scope, frame and tab

tools.name: extract
tools.description: Read repeated non-tabular structures — product cards, list items, search results — as one record per item: item_selector matches the repeating block, fields map output names to selectors relative to it. Read-only, deterministic, parsed server-side from the main-document HTML. Default output: total and shown, then one tab-separated row per item under the field names; a field with no match is empty (null in json).

selector.description: Relative to the item (default: the item itself)

max_items.description: Cap on records returned, in document order

format.description: lines is compact; json keeps one object per record

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

save_to.description: Absolute path: write the records as JSON there and return the path instead of the content

tools.name: assert
tools.description: Assert a page condition, polling until timeout: element exists/visible (optionally with count or containing text), text on page, tab url/title. Patterns: substring, or "/…/" for regex. Recorded flows replay it as a test. Unlike wait_for, which returns found: false, a failure is an error naming what did not match; success returns passed and waited_ms.

selector.description: Element the assertion is about; ">>>" pierces shadow DOM

state.description: attached means present in the DOM, visible also requires a rendered box

text.description: In the element (with selector) or anywhere on the page

timeout.description: Max ms to wait for the condition before failing

tab_id.description: Target tab; omitted = last tab navigated in this session, else the active one

instructions: If the user names another browser tool (e.g. Claude in Chrome) and it is not available, say so and ask; do not switch to chrome-bridge on your own. Several fields: one fill_form (submit_selector submits in the same call), not repeated type_text: one turn instead of N. Tables: extract_table (where/columns filtered server-side) or extract, never read_page: a big table through read_page costs tens of thousands of tokens. Debugging a page: navigate already reports the first console error mapped to its source line and the failed requests with status; get_css_styles names the rule behind a style and flags undefined_vars. Start there; no skill or recipe needed. Detail in a screenshot: element_screenshot (selector or region, scale), not another full one. To check an outcome: assert or wait_for poll for you, no screenshot. When tools are deferred, batch every tool needed for the next workflow into ONE ToolSearch call using exact names (select:name1,name2,...); do not search one tool at a time. Missing optional tools: call get_status({enable:["group",...]}) once for all required groups (audits, visual, network, storage, dom, files, perf; "all" enables all). After tools/list_changed, use them next turn; if still deferred, batch-search their names once. No restart or user configuration needed. Saving a file: never click a Download/Export button and wait for the browser download, the OS "Save as" dialog can open and no tool can press it. A file with a URL: http_request with save_to (browser cookies, bytes written to disk, no dialog). A file the page builds itself (blob, data URL, showSaveFilePicker, a download the page starts): capture_downloads arm, then click, then capture_downloads wait. A tab in a minimized, covered or background window does not render: screenshots fail, timers slow down. get_page_info reports visibility (page_hidden in a result means the same); bring the window on screen, or create_tab new_window with bounds. To find targets use get_interactives, not read_page(html); its refs (n1, n2…) are the ref param of click/type_text/hover and of fill_form fields, and navigate already returns them. tab_id omitted = the tab last navigated/created in this session, else the active tab. frame_id omitted = main frame (list frames with get_frames). Selectors on DOM tools pierce shadow DOM with ">>>" ("my-app >>> button.save").
